sections.h2: Where is Redmond, Oregon, and what kind of place is it?
sections.html:
Redmond is a city in Deschutes County, on the eastern side of the Cascade Range in Oregon's High Desert. It sits at about 3,012 feet, roughly 17 miles north of Bend, which is the county seat. Portland is 146 miles away, Salem 129 miles and Eugene 126 miles.

The city is compact, at about 18.6 square miles, and almost all of it is land. The Horse Lava Tube System runs into the city at the Redmond Caves, a reminder that the ground under many lots here is volcanic rock.

The Census Bureau puts Redmond at 38,547 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 33,274 in the 2020 census and 26,215 in 2010.

sections.h2: How did Redmond grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
Redmond was founded in 1904, platted in 1906 and incorporated on July 6, 1910, and it took its name from Frank T. Redmond, who settled the area in 1905. An irrigation canal built by the company that became part of the Central Oregon Irrigation District made farming and town building possible.

The Oregon Trunk Railway and electric service both arrived in 1911. During the 1940s the city was home to a U.S. Army air base, and commercial flights started at Roberts Field after World War II. The population then sat nearly flat from the 1950s through most of the 1980s.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Redmond, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Redmond has a dry steppe climate with sunny days and cool nights, and the main wear on a house comes from sun, temperature swings and winter freezes. Annual precipitation is only about 8 to 10 inches, which is far drier than the Willamette Valley.

Summer daytime highs usually run from 75 to 100 degrees, and winter highs often sit between 10 and 40. The record high is 119 degrees in August and the record low is minus 28, set in December and January. The growing season is short, since in half of the years from 1971 to 2000 the last freeze came after July 3.

  • Roofing and exterior paint take heavy sun exposure.
  • Pipes, hose bibs and exposed plumbing face hard freezes.
  • Wood decks and fences dry out and crack over the years.
  • Landscaping needs irrigation, so a working sprinkler system is a plus for a buyer.

Fire access has come up locally. At a May 2025 city council hearing on a new subdivision, a nearby resident raised the point that the area had only one good way out in a fire. That resident pointed to the neighborhood's closeness to the urban growth boundary.

sections.h2: What jobs drive the Redmond economy?
sections.html:
Redmond's economy centers on aviation, manufacturing, distribution and tourism around the airport and the surrounding resorts. The city's economic development group, REDI, lists nine target industries.

  • Advanced manufacturing
  • Aviation and aerospace
  • Bioscience and medical devices
  • Brewing and distilling
  • Building products
  • Outdoor and lifestyle products
  • Agricultural products
  • Warehousing and distribution
  • Technology

The Redmond Air Center at the airport is a U.S. Forest Service base for smokejumpers, firefighting and training, and Oregon's only smokejumper base since 1981. Eagle Crest Resort, about 6 miles west of town, is one of eight destination resorts in the state and one of the county's largest corporate taxpayers. REDI also reports a four-year university and a community college in the area, and George Fox University runs a secondary campus in Redmond.

sections.h2: How does Roberts Field affect Redmond house sales?
sections.html:
Roberts Field is Redmond's city-run airport and the only commercial passenger airport in Central Oregon, and it also serves Bend. Alaska, American, Delta and United fly there, and it is the third-busiest commercial airport in Oregon after Portland and Eugene. Passenger traffic reached 1,317,665 in 2025.

A $180 million expansion began in 2025 with federal help. For sellers, the airport is a source of jobs and of out-of-town buyers,, and homes near the flight paths may hear aircraft.

Other transport links are simple. U.S. Route 97 runs north and south through the city on the Redmond Parkway alignment that opened in 2008, Oregon Route 126 meets it and heads west toward Eugene and east to Prineville, and a BNSF main line crosses town. The nearest Amtrak stop is Chemult, about 75 miles south.

sections.h2: Is Redmond adding new houses, and how does that change a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. The Redmond City Council approves new subdivisions under its Redmond 2050 Comprehensive Plan, and recent approvals include a 32-home subdivision called Antelope Flats in southwest Redmond. Groundbreaking was expected six months to a year after approval, with about two years of construction after that.

New supply near your neighborhood can compete with a resale house for the same buyers. It can also bring new streets, utilities and traffic. Staff noted that access on southwest Antelope Avenue did not yet meet partial roadway standards, so road work is part of some projects.

If your house is near open land, check the city's planning pages for pending applications before you set a timeline.

sections.h2: How do Deschutes County property taxes work for a Redmond home?
sections.html:
Deschutes County collects tax on Redmond homes, with payments due November 16, February 16 and May 17 for the 2026-2027 year. Paying in full by November 16 earns a 3 percent discount and paying two-thirds earns 2 percent, while installment payments get no discount. Interest starts to accrue on December 16.

Statements were expected online by October 20 and in the mail by October 25. Mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date, and metered postmarks from mail machines are not accepted. The property tax office is at 1300 NW Wall Street, Suite 203, in Bend, and the phone number is 541-388-6540. There is a drop box in Redmond with limited hours.

Oregon assessed values generally cannot rise more than about 3 percent a year under Measure 50, so a Redmond house owned for many years may carry a low assessed value. Tax proration between buyer and seller is handled through the escrow company at closing. See the Deschutes County payment page for current details.

sections.h2: What must a Redmond seller tell the buyer?
sections.html:
An Oregon seller gives each buyer who makes a written offer a property disclosure statement, and the buyer has five days after delivery to revoke unless that right is waived. The form covers title, water, sewage, structure, systems and general conditions.

Some sellers qualify for exclusions under ORS 105.470, such as a sale by a court-appointed personal representative, trustee or guardian, or a sale by a financial institution after foreclosure. Those sellers complete only Section 1.

faqs.q: How far is Redmond from Bend?
faqs.a: Redmond is about 17 miles north of Bend, which is the Deschutes County seat. Redmond sits at roughly 3,012 feet in the High Desert on the eastern side of the Cascades.

faqs.q: When are Redmond property taxes due?
faqs.a: Deschutes County's 2026-2027 installments are due November 16, February 16 and May 17. A full payment by the first date earns a 3 percent discount, and two-thirds earns 2 percent.

faqs.q: What does the Redmond airport do for the local economy?
faqs.a: It is a hub for jobs and travel. Roberts Field has commercial service from four airlines, and the Redmond Air Center there is a U.S. Forest Service smokejumper and firefighting base.

faqs.q: Does wildfire risk affect selling a house in Redmond?
faqs.a: It can. Residents have raised fire access at a city council hearing, and buyers may ask the same questions. Answer the disclosure form questions honestly and ask your insurer what it needs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Redmond house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is sale is allowed in Oregon, though you still give the buyer the disclosure statement unless an exclusion applies. A cash buyer prices the house in its present condition.
